Volume of Cube = (Side of Cube)3

**Calculation:**

Volume of Cube = (12)³ = 1728 m³

**1728 m³ Volume of air can be contained in the cubical box.**

questions.question: What is the single discount that is equivalent to two successive discounts of 12.5% and 20%?
questions.solution:

Two successive discounts of 12.5% and 20%

**Formula Used:**

x = a+b-(atimes b)/(100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let one discount (a) = 12.5%

⇒ Second discount (b) = 20%

According to the formula,

⇒ x = a+b-(atimes b)/(100)

⇒ x = 12.5+20-(12.5times 20)/(100)=32.5-2.5=30

**Hence, ****The single discount equivalent to two successive discounts of 12.5% and 20% is 30%**

questions.question: The selling price of a book is Rs. 855. If the loss incurred through the sale is 10%, then what is the nominal amount of loss incurred?

Loss% = (loss)/(CP)×100

**Calculation:**

Loss% will be

⇒ Loss% = (loss)/(CP)×100

questions.question: A square of side p is taken. A rectangle is cut out from this square such that the length of one side of the rectangle is equal to half of the length of one side of the square and the length of another side of the rectangle is equal to (1)/(3) of the length of the first side of the rectangle. What is the area of the portion of the square that remained after the rectangle is cut out?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A square of side p is taken

A rectangle is cut out from this square such that the length of one side of the rectangle is equal to half of the length of one side of the square

The length of another side of the rectangle is equal to (1)/(3) the length of the first side of the rectangle

**Formula Used:**

Area of the rectangle = length x breadth

Area of the square = (side)²

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

A rectangle is cut out from this square such that the length of one side of the rectangle is equal to half of the length of one side of the square

⇒ Lenght (l) = (1)/(2)times p=(p)/(2)

⇒ The length of another side of the rectangle is equal to (1)/(3) the length of the first side of the rectangle

⇒ Breath (b) = (1)/(3)times l=(1)/(3)times(p)/(2)=(p)/(6)

⇒ The area of rectangle = l x b = (p)/(2)times (p)/(6)=(p²)/(12)

⇒ The area of square = (side)² = p²

⇒ After the area of the rectangle is cut out from the area of the square, the remaining area is = area of the square - the area of the rectangle = p²-(p²)/(12)=(11p²)/(12)

**Hence, The area of the portion of the square that remained after the rectangle is cut out is (11p²)/(12)**

questions.question: After 4 years, Ramesh's age will be 50% more than what his age was 16 years ago. What is his present age?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Age (after 4 years) to Age (16 years ago) = 150% : 100% = 3 : 2.

Total time gap between the two periods = 4 + 16 = 20 years.

Difference in ratio parts = 3 − 2 = 1 part.

1 part = 20 years ⇒ Age 16 years ago (2 parts) = 20 × 2 = 40 years.

Present age = 40 + 16 = 56 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 56 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

After 4 years, Ramesh's age will be 50% more than what his age was 16 years ago.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f529f6312b6cd3a676c516157317e4d29ce5fbf15a9fb3fd82d98607e0208b73.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the present age of Ramesh be x years.

⇒ Ramesh's age 16 years ago = (x − 16) years

⇒ Ramesh's age after 4 years = (x + 4) years

⇒ Age after 4 years = Age 16 years ago + 50% of Age 16 years ago

⇒ x + 4 = 1.5 × (x − 16)

⇒ x + 4 = 1.5x − 24

⇒ 1.5x − x = 24 + 4

⇒ 0.5x = 28

⇒ x = 28 ÷ 0.5

⇒ x = 56

**∴ The correct answer is 56 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Method for Ages

When comparing ages across different times, the time gap corresponds to the change in ratio parts. Equating the ratio difference to the actual years gap provides the value of 1 ratio part directly.

Handling Percentages in Equations

If a value is P% more than a base value, it is equivalent to (100 + P)% of the base value. Here, 50% more implies 150% of the past age, giving a ratio of 150:100 or 3:2.

Linear Time Gaps

If the present age is x, then the age n years ago is (x − n), and the age m years hence is (x + m). The total time difference between these two points is always (n + m) years.
</p

questions.question: Kajal can do a piece of work alone in 24 days, while Neha can do the same work alone in 40 days. Kajal started the work alone, and then after 12 days, Neha joined her till the completion of the work. How long did the work take to be completed since Kajal started to work on it?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Kajal completes work in = 24 days

Neha can do the same work in = 40 days

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = frac{Total work} {No. of days}

**Calculation:**

Let us assume the total work done be 120 units of work

(We can assume any number, but for the sake of easy calculation, it is advised to take L.C.M. of the given numbers. Here, the number given are 24 and 40)

Now, Kajal completes work in = 24 days

⇒ Efficiency of Kajal = (Total work)/(No. of days) = (120)/(24) = 5 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of Neha = (Total work)/(No. of days) = (120)/(40) = 3 units/day 

⇒ As, given in the question, Kajal worked for 12 days, before Neha

⇒ Work done by Kajal = Efficiency × No. of days = 5 × 12 = 60 units

Hence, 60 units of work are done by Kajal alone, 

⇒ Remaining work = (120 - 60) = 60 unit

⇒ Combined Efficiency of Kajal and Neha = (5 + 3) = 8 units/day

⇒ No. of days = (60)/(8) days = (15)/(2) days

⇒ Total number of days = 12 + (15)/(2) = (39)/(2) days.

**Hence, the work will take** (39)/(2)** days to complete since Kajal started working.**

questions.question: In what time does a sum of money amount to twice of itself at the simple interest of 25% per annum?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a sum becomes **n** times of itself at Simple Interest rate **R%**, the time **T** is given by:

T = [(n − 1) × 100] ÷ R

Here, n = 2 (since it becomes twice) and R = 25%.

⇒ T = [(2 − 1) × 100] ÷ 25

⇒ T = 100 ÷ 25 = 4 years

**∴ The correct answer is 4 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rate of Interest (R) = 25% per annum

Let the Principal (P) be 100 units.

Since the sum amounts to twice itself, Amount (A) = 2 × 100 = 200 units.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = Amount − Principal

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Start (t = 0)
 End (t = ?)
 
 P = 100 units
 A = 200 units
 
 
 

 

 
 
 SI = +100 units
 Rate = 25% p.a.

**Calculation:**

⇒ SI = 200 − 100 = 100 units

⇒ 100 = (100 × 25 × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 100 = 25 × T

⇒ T = 100 ÷ 25

⇒ T = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum becoming 'n' times (Rate Calculation)

If a sum becomes 'n' times of itself in 'T' years at simple interest, the rate can be found directly by: R = [(n − 1) × 100] ÷ T.

Direct Amount Formula for SI

The total amount A after T years can be calculated as: A = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Rule of 72

A general financial shortcut used to estimate the time required to double an investment when the interest is compounded: Time ≈ 72 ÷ R. However, for Simple Interest, the exact doubling time is always 100 ÷ R.
</p
